name: ACoRNE
summary: A UK feasibility programme used the Rona naval hydrophone array off northwest Scotland to study acoustic detection of ultra-high-energy neutrinos, backgrounds, calibration and signal reconstruction.
detection_principle: Rapid cascade heating in water can generate a bipolar acoustic pulse. Continuously recorded hydrophone signals were analysed with matched filters, spectral filters and coincidences to separate possible cascade-like pulses from biological and environmental noise.
technologies: Thermo-acoustic particle detection with hydrophones or piezoelectric sensors

sites.name: Rona naval hydrophone range, northwest Scotland
sites.location: Rona naval hydrophone range, northwest Scotland

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The archive records a historical R&D programme documented by 2005–2008 campaigns; no present-day full-scale neutrino observatory is established.

timeline.event: First dedicated acoustic-neutrino feasibility data recorded at Rona.
Initial array performance and signal-processing results published.

key_parameters.name: 2005 readout
key_parameters.value: Eight hydrophones; 140 kHz sampling with 16-bit precision

key_parameters.name: Array scale
key_parameters.value: Approximately 1.5 km long in water approximately 230 m deep

key_parameters.name: First recording
key_parameters.value: 15 days in December 2005, yielding approximately 2.8 TB

results.summary: Initial data demonstrated continuous recording and background-filtering methods. Published sensitivity estimates are not a confirmed acoustic-neutrino observation.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
